faq.q: What kinds of passwords can it make?
faq.a: Five modes: Random (length 4–128 with A–Z, a–z, 0–9 and a customisable symbol set), Passphrase (3–8 words from a built-in list with your choice of separator and case, optionally appending digits), PIN (3–12 digits, optionally avoiding obvious sequences like 1234 or 1111), Memorable (pronounceable consonant-vowel syllables), and a Checker that analyses a password you paste.

Yes. Every mode uses crypto.getRandomValues() with rejection sampling for uniform, unbiased output — not Math.random(). For Random mode you can require one of each selected character type, forbid repeated characters, exclude ambiguous characters (0 O 1 l I), and exclude specific characters; the tool explains clearly if your constraints can't be met at the chosen length.

faq.q: How does the strength meter work?
faq.a: It calculates entropy in bits from the password length and character-set size (or word-list size for passphrases), then scores Weak/Fair/Good/Strong. It flags common passwords, repeated characters, keyboard walks, dates/years and dictionary words, downgrading the score when found. It also shows estimated crack times under three scenarios: throttled online (100/s), bcrypt (10K/s) and fast SHA-256 (10 billion/s).

faq.q: Does it store or send my passwords?
faq.a: No passwords leave your browser and none are sent to any server. Only generator options (length, checkboxes, symbol set) are saved to local storage; generated passwords, bulk output, the Checker input and the recent list are deliberately never stored. Recent passwords live only in sessionStorage (last 5, cleared when the tab closes). Bulk mode can make up to 500 at once and download them as a .txt.
